primitives.name: PageRank Algorithm
primitives.verbatim_quote: (57) ABSTRACT A method assigns importance ranks to nodes in a linked database, such as any database of documents containing citations, the world wide web or any other hypermedia database.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'r': 'vector of node ranks (dimensionless)', 'd': 'damping factor (dimensionless, typically 0.85)', 'M': 'transition probability matrix (dimensionless)', 'n': 'number of nodes (dimensionless)', '1': 'vector of ones (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Graph is strongly connected, damping factor ensures convergence, all nodes have equal initial rank.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When graph contains disconnected components or sink nodes, convergence may fail without proper damping.

layer2.mapping: The PageRank vector corresponds to the stationary distribution of a Markov chain defined by the hyperlink structure, enabling probabilistic inference in GSI and deterministic state transitions in GSE.
layer2.telemetry: Node rank stability over iterations, convergence rate, and hyperlink entropy.

primitives.name: Citation Network Centralization
primitives.verbatim_quote: Garfield, "Citation analysis as a tool in journal evaluation," 1972, Science, vol.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'C': 'centralization coefficient (dimensionless)', 'k_i': 'degree of node i (dimensionless)', '\\bar{k}': 'mean degree (dimensionless)', 'n': 'total number of nodes (dimensionless)', '\\sigma^2': 'variance of degrees (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Network is undirected, node degrees follow a normal distribution around mean.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When network exhibits high variance or non-normal degree distribution, centralization measure becomes unreliable.

layer2.mapping: Centralization score informs GSI's confidence in citation-based relevance signals and GSE's prioritization of highly cited nodes during traversal.
layer2.telemetry: Degree variance across nodes, normalized centralization index, and citation density.

primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'H': 'connectivity entropy (dimensionless)', 'w_{ij}': 'weight of hyperlink from i to j (dimensionless)', 'w_{avg}': 'average hyperlink weight (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Link weights are positive and normalized, logarithmic scaling captures information content.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of PageRank lies in modeling the web as a directed graph where each page is a node and each hyperlink is an edge. The algorithm assumes that a page is important if it is linked to by other important pages. This leads to a recursive definition of importance, solved iteratively via a Markov chain. The damping factor d models the probability that a user will continue clicking links versus jumping to a random page. The convergence of the rank vector r is guaranteed under standard conditions due to the ergodicity of the transition matrix M. In GSI, this translates into a Bayesian update mechanism over belief states, where each node’s rank becomes a posterior probability. In GSE, it enables a state transition model where traversal decisions are made based on current rank estimates. Citation networks extend this idea by treating citations as links, allowing for a similar centrality-based ranking. The centralization measure provides a way to assess how much influence is concentrated among a few nodes, which can be used to detect anomalies or hubs in the network. Hyperlink connectivity index adds another layer by measuring the diversity of link structures, helping identify dense clusters or sparse regions in the graph. These primitives form a layered system where PageRank provides the base importance metric, citation centralization offers robustness checks, and hyperlink connectivity refines navigation strategies.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: Rooted in early sociometric studies by Katz (1953) and Hubbell (1965), the concept evolved through citation analysis by Garfield (1972) and Pinski/Narin (1976). The formalization of centrality in networks was further developed by Mizruchi et al. (1996) and Ramer et al. (1996). The PageRank algorithm directly builds upon these foundations, applying them to the web graph structure. reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: Opposing agents include users who may navigate randomly or follow links arbitrarily, and search engines aiming to surface relevant content. The algorithm must balance between capturing true relevance and avoiding manipulation through artificial link farms. In adversarial settings, nodes might attempt to game the system by creating fake links or exploiting citation patterns, necessitating robustness checks in both GSI and GSE layers.
